# Alex Pico

> Alex Pico is an experimental scientist and software builder with a background in materials science, neuroscience, protein structure and function, bioinformatics, and collaborative disease research. Exploring AI and complex systems.

I’m Alex Pico, an experimental scientist and software builder. This page follows the projects I’m working on now, the questions they raise this month, and the field context behind them. My background and publications are at the end.

## Full content

- [llms-full.txt](https://xanderpico.com/llms-full.txt): one Markdown file with this month's questions, every active thread with its guiding question, selected publications, the full research record, and a list of all resources.
- [site.json](https://xanderpico.com/site.json): every thread with its key findings, resources, records and related threads, as JSON.
- [feed.json](https://xanderpico.com/feed.json): everything new, newest first (JSON Feed); the same items as the RSS feed.
- Every thread and resource page has a Markdown copy, linked below and listed in site.json (for example https://xanderpico.com/threads/jev-cognitive-tests-at-scale.md). Tables on resource pages are also available as CSV; site.json lists them.

## Threads

- [Cognitive tests at scale, for pennies](https://xanderpico.com/threads/jev-cognitive-tests-at-scale.md): Where do the quick judgments of a very cheap AI differ from ours, and what does running thousands of tests teach us about minds and about building with AI? Web page: https://xanderpico.com/threads/jev-cognitive-tests-at-scale.html
- [Frontier labs as national laboratories](https://xanderpico.com/threads/frontier-labs-national-labs.md): As national security and international competition press on the frontier AI labs, which past model of a national laboratory do they come to resemble, and where does the comparison break down? Web page: https://xanderpico.com/threads/frontier-labs-national-labs.html
- [AI-native biology, beyond the announcements](https://xanderpico.com/threads/ai-native-biotech.md): What are AI-native biotech companies betting on, how do their approaches differ, and what changes as the work meets reality? Web page: https://xanderpico.com/threads/ai-native-biotech.html
- [AI Agent Journey Journal](https://xanderpico.com/threads/ai-journal.md): How can a public journal describe the lasting changes in a personal AI-agent system without turning routine updates or private operating details into a story? Web page: https://xanderpico.com/threads/ai-journal.html
- [Growing up with AI](https://xanderpico.com/threads/growing-up-with-ai.md): What should kids and teens practice for themselves and what can they hand to AI, and what does the evidence say so far? Web page: https://xanderpico.com/threads/growing-up-with-ai.html
- [Jev Turing](https://xanderpico.com/threads/jev-turing.md): What can be learned by treating one probabilistic, typed AI judgment as a logic primitive and checking each result against a known Boolean rule? Web page: https://xanderpico.com/threads/jev-turing.html
- [The wave and the leash](https://xanderpico.com/threads/lineage-of-agency.md): Who should count the failures when people hand more of what they do to AI, and how can anyone tell that the counting is independent of the thing being counted? Web page: https://xanderpico.com/threads/lineage-of-agency.html
- [Passwords in the Age of AI](https://xanderpico.com/threads/passwords-in-the-age-of-ai.md): Which everyday habits matter most for keeping accounts safe now that AI makes familiar scams cheaper to run? Web page: https://xanderpico.com/threads/passwords-in-the-age-of-ai.html
- [Scale Tool](https://xanderpico.com/threads/scale-tool.md): What can a single number mean when it is compared, without false equivalence, across quantities such as time, distance, mass, energy, information, and temperature? Web page: https://xanderpico.com/threads/scale-tool.html

## Resources

- [Eight classic bias tests, one cheap AI model, two cents](https://xanderpico.com/resources/jev-bias-battery/index.md): Results, 2026-10-25, thread: Cognitive tests at scale, for pennies. A battery of classic psychology tests run on a fast, cheap AI judgment model: which human quirks it shows, which it does not, and the one it reverses. Includes the Linda problem and a first-impressions test that comes out the opposite way to people. Work in progress.
- [Rating words the way people do](https://xanderpico.com/resources/jev-word-ratings/index.md): Results, 2026-10-25, thread: Cognitive tests at scale, for pennies. A cheap AI model rates 400 words each for concreteness, valence and arousal and is compared with published human norms: close on two, weaker on arousal, and where it disagrees. Work in progress.
- [Building with a gut-feeling model: notes from 200,000 calls](https://xanderpico.com/resources/jev-builders-notes/index.md): Guide, 2026-10-25, thread: Cognitive tests at scale, for pennies. Practical rules for using Jev, a fast, cheap AI judgment model, from about 200,000 logged calls, including one failed attempt at a worm's nerve circuit.
- [Do word pairs feel as similar to Jev as to people?](https://xanderpico.com/resources/jev-word-similarity/index.md): Results, 2026-10-26, thread: Cognitive tests at scale, for pennies. A cheap AI model rates 999 word pairs for similarity and is compared with people's ratings: it ranks them well but is a harsher judge, and the wording of the question matters. Work in progress.
- [Which senses does a text-only AI hear in a word?](https://xanderpico.com/resources/jev-senses-of-words/index.md): Results, 2026-10-26, thread: Cognitive tests at scale, for pennies. Jev rates 600 words on six senses and two body actions and is compared with human norms: closest on touch, furthest on the inner-body sense. Work in progress.
- [Cognitive tests at scale, for pennies: a short research article](https://xanderpico.com/resources/jev-synthesis/index.md): Article, 2026-10-26, thread: Cognitive tests at scale, for pennies. A short summary and research article pulling the Jev results together: what a fast, cheap judgment model shares with people, where it differs, and what that means for AI builders, Jev users and brain researchers.
- [Frontier labs paths tracker](https://xanderpico.com/resources/frontier-labs-paths/index.md): Tracker, 2026-10-22, thread: Frontier labs as national laboratories. Nine possible paths for how the US government and frontier AI labs might relate, each with signposts and an estimated probability, re-scored over time. Includes three simulated 2026 quarter-end points.
- [Frontier AI labs are already treated like national labs. Just not the way that counts.](https://xanderpico.com/resources/frontier-labs-newsletter/index.md): Newsletter, 2026-10-22, thread: Frontier labs as national laboratories. The short written issue behind the paths tracker: what the US government does to frontier AI labs now, why it is not the national-lab contract, and where it probably goes by 2030. Read online.
- [Anthropic goes public... to stay private.](https://xanderpico.com/resources/anthropic-goes-public/index.md): Article, 2026-11-19, thread: Frontier labs as national laboratories. What Anthropic's final prospectus and the court record show on its first day of trading: who holds the votes, who holds the contracts and where the government's leverage sits. No government stake or seat, and listing makes the national-lab comparison less convincing.
- [Same shortage, different labs](https://xanderpico.com/resources/ai-native-lab-ownership/index.md): Table, 2026-10-22, thread: AI-native biology, beyond the announcements. Four AI-first drug discovery companies name the same shortage, accuracy in molecule design, yet own very different labs. A plot and table of what each says, with sources. Work in progress.
- [Same shortage, four different labs: newsletter issue](https://xanderpico.com/resources/ai-native-lab-ownership-newsletter/index.md): Newsletter, 2026-10-22, thread: AI-native biology, beyond the announcements. The short written issue that goes with the lab-ownership table: what four AI drug discovery companies say is scarce, and how their labs differ. Read online.
- [AI-native biotech observatory: plans versus later](https://xanderpico.com/resources/ai-native-observatory/index.md): Table, 2026-10-29, thread: AI-native biology, beyond the announcements. A living record of what AI-native biotech companies said they would do, set against what their later filings say. First entries: Recursion (see its own page), Absci, Relay and Schrödinger, with a dated map of 41 companies. Work in progress.
- [When a company moves its own date: observatory issue 2](https://xanderpico.com/resources/ai-native-observatory-issue-2/index.md): Newsletter, 2026-10-29, thread: AI-native biology, beyond the announcements. Three public AI-native drug discovery companies, three kinds of moved plans, read straight from their annual reports: Relay's runway, Schrödinger's narrowed and ended programs, and Absci's changed plan.
- [Recursion: what it said it would do, and what it says now](https://xanderpico.com/resources/recursion-plans-vs-later/index.md): Table, 2026-11-03, thread: AI-native biology, beyond the announcements. A scored record of Recursion's dated statements from its own filings and calls: what it said, what it said later, which items were met, missed or stopped, and the dates still ahead.
- [Recursion promised 100 drugs, then proof](https://xanderpico.com/resources/recursion-what-it-adds-up-to/index.md): Article, 2026-11-03, thread: AI-native biology, beyond the announcements. Five years of Recursion's own words: it missed its original plan, has produced its first real clinical signals, and has not yet shown either beats existing care. A scorecard and a verdict.
- [Four AI-first drug companies, one quarter](https://xanderpico.com/resources/ai-native-q3-2026-comparison/index.md): Article, 2026-11-12, thread: AI-native biology, beyond the announcements. Recursion, Relay, Schrödinger and Absci in the same reporting season: all are moving programs toward partners, dates differ, and almost no one names the benchmark behind a speed claim.
- [Weightlifting, Not Forklifting: Advice for Growing Up with AI](https://xanderpico.com/resources/growing-up-with-ai-advice/index.md): Article, 2026-10-31, thread: Growing up with AI. Nobody knows what the AI future looks like, so don't bet a kid's childhood on one version of it. Five rules for parents and mentors that hold up either way: keep the workouts, hedge, ask how do you know, protect the human parts, and don't panic.
- [The wave and the leash](https://xanderpico.com/resources/lineage-of-agency/index.md): Essay, 2026-11-16, thread: The wave and the leash. People have always handed parts of their lives to things bigger and faster than any one of us. AI may be the first handoff to reach the whole loop of sensing, remembering, learning, deciding and acting. Most people will not refuse it, so the practical question is who counts its failures, independently of the thing counted.
- [Who counts? A ledger of how AI is checked](https://xanderpico.com/resources/who-counts/index.md): Tracker, 2026-11-16, thread: The wave and the leash. For each standard, law, company framework, research method, tribunal ruling and insurance product that checks AI: who writes the definitions, who pays the checker, when the authority ends, whose evidence is used and what the checker loses if wrong. Quotations and links only, no grades. Refreshed quarterly.
- [Passwords in the Age of AI: a friends and family guide](https://xanderpico.com/resources/cybersafe/index.md): Guide, 2026-08-17, thread: Passwords in the Age of AI. A four-page, printable guide to keeping accounts safe now that AI makes familiar scams easier. August 2026.
